headline: Bitcoin clears $81,000 and Zcash hits $1,000 as record ETF inflows fuel a broad crypto rally
summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled in $731 million in a single day — the largest inflow since January — pushing BTC above $81,000 and lifting nearly every major asset. Zcash was the standout, surging 20% to breach the $1,000 mark as a short squeeze wiped out $34 million in bearish bets. Privacy coins led the charge, but the rally was broad: Ethereum gained 5.4%, XRP climbed 6.2%, and Hyperliquid rose nearly 7%.

winners.name: Zcash
winners.catalyst: A short squeeze liquidated roughly $34 million in short positions, driving ZEC to the psychologically significant $1,000 level. The move was amplified by broad privacy-coin momentum and improving market sentiment tied to fading Fed rate-hike odds and record Bitcoin ETF inflows.

losers.name: LEO Token
losers.catalyst: No specific catalyst identified; LEO was the weakest performer on the day, slipping 1.2% while the broader market rallied.

whyItMoved:
The day's main engine was institutional money flowing back into Bitcoin ETFs at a scale not seen since January. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $731 million in net inflows on September 4 — a single-day figure that signals a meaningful return of fund-level demand, not just retail enthusiasm. That inflow pushed BTC above $81,000 and set the tone for everything else.

Layered on top of that was a shift in expectations around Federal Reserve policy. Fading odds of another rate hike made risk assets broadly more attractive, and crypto — which tends to move sharply when macro headwinds ease — responded across the board. Ethereum gained 5.4%, XRP climbed 6.2%, Dogecoin rose 5.8%, and Hyperliquid added nearly 7%.

The sharpest move belonged to Zcash, which surged 20% to breach $1,000 for the first time. The immediate trigger was a short squeeze: traders who had bet against ZEC were forced to buy back their positions as the price rose, accelerating the move. Roughly $34 million in short positions were liquidated in the process. Monero gained 7.4% on the same session, suggesting broader momentum behind privacy-focused coins rather than a Zcash-specific story. The Fear & Greed Index sits at 74 — firmly in Greed territory — reflecting the day's risk-on tone.
worthKnowing: OpenReserve, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, received preliminary approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to operate as a national bank — a significant step toward blockchain-native firms holding full banking licenses in the US.

South Korea announced a phased plan to launch a fully tokenized securities market by February 2027, covering all asset classes and reinforcing the global push toward regulated on-chain capital markets.
Monero (XMR) gained 7.4% alongside Zcash's 20% surge, suggesting the session's privacy-coin rally was broad rather than isolated to a single asset.
